title: Beyond Realism: From 2D Concept to Immersive 3D Environments with Marvelous Designer
content:
## _Discover how Turkish indie game developer_[ _Ufuk Karapicak_](https://www.artstation.com/cubesugar) _uses Marvelous Designer to craft immersive 3D worlds brimming with imagination and storytelling._

![cd2c628798ae4658bbe789d6caad973e](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/db9eacf6ce2740f5b4f89940d0548bee/images/cd2c628798ae4658bbe789d6caad973eufuk-karapicak-bms-watervillage-55.jpg)![d7b79fce90e241d7bbf7b25b8cba1297](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/db9eacf6ce2740f5b4f89940d0548bee/images/d7b79fce90e241d7bbf7b25b8cba1297ufuk-karapicak-bms-watervillage-3.jpg)

My name is Ufuk Karapicak, and I’m an environment artist and indie game developer based in Turkey.

I started out doing 2D concept art, but over time I became more and more curious about 3D. That curiosity first led me into 3D concept art, and eventually into game art, where I found the perfect space to combine imagination, storytelling, and technical creation.

Now, as an indie developer, I focus on building my own worlds, places that feel alive and carry emotion through design.

What motivates me the most is the idea of inspiring others — to show that even as a single artist, it’s possible to bring your vision to life and maybe spark the same motivation in someone else. Art and games have always given me strength; I hope what I create can give a little of that back.

# **How did you use Marvelous Designer in the artwork?**

In this project, which I worked on while I was part of Big Medium Small, the concept by Kay Tang depicted a world where people live side by side with water — everything around them is shaped by moisture, wind, and time.

To capture that feeling, I used Marvelous Designer to create all the fabric-related elements in the scene: rice sacks piled on boats, tarps stretched over wooden surfaces, and scattered pieces of worn cloth.

![0ad81cd60e5a48cd97083e472a1e9322](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/db9eacf6ce2740f5b4f89940d0548bee/images/0ad81cd60e5a48cd97083e472a1e9322ufuk-karapicak-bms-watervillage-43.jpg)

![c25f93ac1fa74274bd2e6d6889452c2c](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/db9eacf6ce2740f5b4f89940d0548bee/images/c25f93ac1fa74274bd2e6d6889452c2cimage%20%289%29.png)

![2382de218c8a4626bb97eadedff5a51d](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/db9eacf6ce2740f5b4f89940d0548bee/images/2382de218c8a4626bb97eadedff5a51dufuk-karapicak-bms-watervillage-7.jpg)

Each fabric had to feel lived in, not just physically accurate, but emotionally believable.

I imagined how these people might have reused the same materials over years; some fabrics looked freshly replaced, while others carried dirt, folds, and wear from long use.

Marvelous Designer allowed me to express those subtle differences with real motion and natural imperfections.

Sculpting them by hand wouldn’t have captured that sense of history — Marvelous let me design through movement, as if I were watching the fabrics live in the world I was creating.

# Why did you decide to use Marvelous Designer? How did it help you serve art direction?

I chose Marvelous Designer for this project because it combines precision with creativity in a way that no other tool does.  
Over the years, I’ve realized how much freedom it gives me — not only to simulate cloth accurately, but to design through simulation.  
It naturally encourages a procedural mindset— I’m not just modeling shapes, I’m _discovering_ them through motion, gravity, and tension.  
That way of working keeps the creative process fluid and open to new ideas.

![372bb59554e34975844bf1410f98ec33](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/db9eacf6ce2740f5b4f89940d0548bee/images/372bb59554e34975844bf1410f98ec33image%20%2853%29.png)

One of the biggest advantages for me is how easily I can respond to feedback.  
Marvelous Designer allows extremely fast iteration — I can test, adjust, and see the results almost instantly, which makes the art direction process much more organic.  
It helps me focus on form, proportion, and flow rather than getting stuck in technical constraints.

![600f3247e6f2428bbb59a7f82ca736c2](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/db9eacf6ce2740f5b4f89940d0548bee/images/600f3247e6f2428bbb59a7f82ca736c2image%20%2857%29.png)![cb39b22e3bd043d19c7054c533a5c644](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/db9eacf6ce2740f5b4f89940d0548bee/images/cb39b22e3bd043d19c7054c533a5c644image%20%286%29.png)![4aeb98eb0ed545e7880bc777e55d6c2d](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/db9eacf6ce2740f5b4f89940d0548bee/images/4aeb98eb0ed545e7880bc777e55d6c2dufuk-karapicak-bms-watervillage-18.jpg)

And then there are those _happy accidents_ — when the fabric behaves unexpectedly but beautifully.  
Those moments often inspire new artistic directions.  
Marvelous Designer gives me both speed and depth: I can work like a designer, but think like a storyteller.  
That balance is what keeps me using it in every project.

# Do you have any other projects that you have worked on using Marvelous Designer that you can share with us?

![c708beb932744196b642a04d8c89229b](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/db9eacf6ce2740f5b4f89940d0548bee/images/c708beb932744196b642a04d8c89229bufuk-karapicak-mysticscene-low.jpg)![861639a2f0024939b5e69f628e1fd68d](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/db9eacf6ce2740f5b4f89940d0548bee/images/861639a2f0024939b5e69f628e1fd68dufuk-karapicak-artnouveupetshopsmallsize.jpg)

Before this project, I had been using **Marvelous Designer** for years in my concept art and illustration work.  
I often built 3D blockouts, draped clothes on Daz3D models or my own rigs, and painted over them.  
It helped me quickly find shapes and silhouettes that felt alive — almost like painting in 3D.  
Those experiments taught me how much Marvelous Designer could serve creativity, not just realism.

![05deb1f6178e4092bcd860d83e6258f5](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/db9eacf6ce2740f5b4f89940d0548bee/images/05deb1f6178e4092bcd860d83e6258f5ufuk-karapicak-scene-01-02.jpg)![da9d39f870274cd98f1c0d30c127451f](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/db9eacf6ce2740f5b4f89940d0548bee/images/da9d39f870274cd98f1c0d30c127451fufuk-karapicak-centercompfin-03.jpg)Now, as an **indie game developer** , I plan to explore it much more deeply — using advanced simulations, complex setups, and character-based storytelling.

# Can you give us a quick overview of the different tools used in your pipeline?

In most of my 3D projects, I use Marvelous Designer, Blender, ZBrush, Substance Painter, and Substance Designer as my main tools.  
There isn’t always a fixed order — I follow the general workflow you’d expect, but I also move between programs depending on what the project needs.

If I’m creating an illustration, I sometimes use Daz3D for quick posing, or I rig and animate directly in Blender.  
I often export certain poses from Blender into Marvelous Designer to run different fabric simulations, then bring the results back into Blender for rendering.  
In some cases, I even turn the fabrics I make in Marvelous Designer into brush alphas for sculpting in ZBrush or texturing in Substance Painter.

I really enjoy this fluid workflow because it lets me use each software for what it does best — Marvelous Designer for believable forms and motion, ZBrush for detail, Substance for materials, and Blender or Unreal for lighting and presentation.

# Are there any tips and tricks with Marvelous Designer that you can share with the community?

![11ae02031774443f8924a49938530500](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/db9eacf6ce2740f5b4f89940d0548bee/images/11ae02031774443f8924a49938530500ufuk-karapicak-bms-watervillage-38.jpg)![be9a14fd8752419f9c536985c39d7e7e](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/db9eacf6ce2740f5b4f89940d0548bee/images/be9a14fd8752419f9c536985c39d7e7eimage%20%287%29.png)![383c97f1adbf43e58b7d43aa310f997a](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/db9eacf6ce2740f5b4f89940d0548bee/images/383c97f1adbf43e58b7d43aa310f997aimage%20%2811%29.png)![4cb351a40ace48fa9cea963d962ca8ed](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/db9eacf6ce2740f5b4f89940d0548bee/images/4cb351a40ace48fa9cea963d962ca8edimage%20%2812%29.png)

I’m not an expert, but I’d like to share something that really helped me — especially for beginners.

When I first started using Marvelous Designer, I was honestly scared of breaking things.

I kept my designs very simple and avoided pushing the simulation too far.

But later, I began to experiment more — I exaggerated folds, pushed the limits of the simulation, and stopped worrying about being “correct.”

That’s when I truly started to learn.

Marvelous Designer became much more fun and expressive once I let go of that fear.

I hope this helps someone who’s just starting out — don’t be afraid to play with it. That’s how you discover what makes it powerful.

title: Indie Spotlight: Spencer on Building 'Rhythm Towers' with Marvelous Designer
content:
## ![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/eecbfe44fe5d43b5b0b001bba745af0f/images/27780ef0e11d4159916a1e6df2d2c625769c0b5484b8f325d52ffcbde516cd2e88740e34c783b208.png)_Unlock the Marvelous Designer to Unreal Engine Chaos Cloth pipeline. Spencer, founder of innoloop, creator of an indie game Rhythm Towers, gives us a masterclass in his workflow, sharing the exact steps and "gotchas" for bringing Marvelous Designer garments to life with real-time physics in Unreal._

* * *

YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hgquCxhWqZ0?start=0

# **Interview with Spencer Beckford |**[**Rhythm Towers**](https://rhythmtowers.com/)**| Founder of**[** _Innoloop_**](https://www.innoloop.com/)

* * *

# **Could you please start by telling us a bit about yourself and your game, Rhythm Towers?**

Hi! I’m Spencer, founder of [_innoloop_](https://www.innoloop.com/), a small indie game studio based in the UK. I’m a former software engineer who decided in 2017 to learn a whole new bunch of creative skills: drawing, painting, sculpting, character modeling, animation, sound design, music composition, and level design so I could build my own games and create my own worlds. When the 2020 lockdowns hit, I asked myself “if not now, when?” and committed fully to game development.

Rhythm Towers is a love letter to two genres I adore, rhythm action and strategy - set on a funky alien world where music powers everything. 

![1f52349bf9954eaf9c6ced28c2c3dc39](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/ce320914f6c243e1b38299ebd6b26ddf/images/1f52349bf9954eaf9c6ced28c2c3dc39769c0b5484b8f325d52ffcbde516cd2e88740e34c783b208.png)

The first prototype was built in Dreams on PlayStation 4; early feedback from friends and players in the Dreamiverse convinced me to take it further, so I migrated to Unreal Engine and began production with an enthusiasm that I still have to this day! 

![d09a0282d72445cebdf04d21e4b2563d](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/ce320914f6c243e1b38299ebd6b26ddf/images/d09a0282d72445cebdf04d21e4b2563dscreen_2.png)

![1def1575b0214fcc8bf9940c2b33c6dd](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/ce320914f6c243e1b38299ebd6b26ddf/images/1def1575b0214fcc8bf9940c2b33c6ddscreen_1.png)

You can play the public demo on [_Steam_](https://store.steampowered.com/app/1561030/Rhythm_Towers/), [_Epic_](https://store.epicgames.com/p/rhythm-towers-c3ef51), and [_Xbox_](https://www.xbox.com/games/store/rhythm-towers/9phg9wljtfbh) Series X|S, with [_PlayStation_](https://store.playstation.com/concept/10003390/)[ _5_](https://store.playstation.com/zh-hant-hk/concept/10003390/) coming soon (hopefully within the next month, and it may even be live by the time this interview goes up). I’m always listening for feedback, so the community on [Discord](https://discord.gg/8YDxytt) and people that play the game at live showcases have shaped a surprising amount of the game.

# **Could you give us an overview of the game's story and its core gameplay experience?**

Welcome to Planet Rhapsody, a vibrant and harmonious land powered by a mystical musical entity called the AlgoRhythm. All was well until an invading noise-hating species known as the Creeps set upon it to silence it for good. You and your misfit band of alien buddies, known for their rhythmic dance moves, become its budding defenders.

![55e65bff6d4f419480d235fd8272c3d1](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/ce320914f6c243e1b38299ebd6b26ddf/images/55e65bff6d4f419480d235fd8272c3d1screen_7.png)Moment to moment, the game blends**rhythm-action with tactical tower placement.** You place Rhythm Towers along the Creeps’ paths to stop them from reaching the AlgoRhythm, but each build is “paid for” by playing a short rhythmic phrase. Your performance on the rhythm matching determines the strength/speed/range of your towers and also layers into the dynamic soundtrack that reacts to your play. You can play solo, couch co-op split-screen, or online co-op, coordinating builds and harmonizing playstyles as the Creeps escalate and demand new tactics.

# ![db01daca900b416299d9a71b1023aae1](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/ce320914f6c243e1b38299ebd6b26ddf/images/db01daca900b416299d9a71b1023aae1screen_8.png)![e84795ee1b6a4e5aad1879af04465209](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/ce320914f6c243e1b38299ebd6b26ddf/images/e84795ee1b6a4e5aad1879af04465209screen_9.png)

# **From the in-game scenes, we noticed that the character animations are very dynamic, and the clothing moves naturally with them. Could you walk us through your workflow for character animation?**

**Concept art & design (Adobe Photoshop)**

  * Character bios/personality (Big Five), silhouette sketches, color proofs, and final paint-overs to achieve the read of each character at a gameplay distance. 




![c649a79606814b568300af40ebeef3b3](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/ce320914f6c243e1b38299ebd6b26ddf/images/c649a79606814b568300af40ebeef3b3spencer%20ppt2.png)![a1eebcdc16ac4eea867ced0f1fab51b9](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/ce320914f6c243e1b38299ebd6b26ddf/images/a1eebcdc16ac4eea867ced0f1fab51b9spencer%20ppt3.png)

**Body modeling (Character Creator → ZBrush)**

  * Start on a Character Creator base (I previously used CC4, and have now migrated to CC5 for its UE5-ready skeleton support), use simple morphs and skingen to get close to the concept.

  * GoZ round-trips to ZBrush to sculpt features and tertiary details; facial morphs for expression range.

  * Export FBX.




![0e72c1344c6848fdb775f31163421316](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/ce320914f6c243e1b38299ebd6b26ddf/images/0e72c1344c6848fdb775f31163421316spencer%20ppt4.png)![ba6c54ed158b461092cfbf58f0d37c51](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/ce320914f6c243e1b38299ebd6b26ddf/images/ba6c54ed158b461092cfbf58f0d37c51spencer%20ppt5.png)

**Garments (Marvelous Designer)**

  * Pattern making and sewing following the concept art: add buttons, zips, internal lines, top stitches for detailing.

  * Simulation passes to quickly test range of motion (walks, fast turns, jumps, dance steps), iterate on fabric properties for the right bounce/drag.




![8a75a3381b07420bbbdb24f47b1c6f6a](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/ce320914f6c243e1b38299ebd6b26ddf/images/8a75a3381b07420bbbdb24f47b1c6f6aSpencer_PPT%206.png)![a38c30a1d6db49db98d589e9be59f4a8](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/ce320914f6c243e1b38299ebd6b26ddf/images/a38c30a1d6db49db98d589e9be59f4a8Spencer_PPT7.png)

  * UVs & ID maps to help the material/texture workflow later on.




![2279321fc2d8414cb388d5709a26d637](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/ce320914f6c243e1b38299ebd6b26ddf/images/2279321fc2d8414cb388d5709a26d637Spencer_PPT8.png)

  * USD export (plus garment simulation data) to keep the Unreal import predictable.




### **Shoes (Blender)**

  * SubD box-modeling; create UVs, use vertex colors to create ID maps.




![944c7c3ac0da44b2b3eab866c52355eb](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/ce320914f6c243e1b38299ebd6b26ddf/images/944c7c3ac0da44b2b3eab866c52355ebSpencer_PPT9.png)

**Surface detail (Substance 3D Painter)**

  * Bake mesh maps; use ID maps for fast material assignments. Add decals and story-driven wear.




![e2c3ef4994b64529b1c00a2fcd34f741](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/ce320914f6c243e1b38299ebd6b26ddf/images/e2c3ef4994b64529b1c00a2fcd34f741Spencer_PPT10.png)

### **Motion Capture (Move.ai & Cascadeur)**

  * 4 x iPhones for motion capture via Move.ai for base motions and dance moves; Cascadeur for mocap cleanup, timing, looping and stylized exaggeration.




![9e0829532c344ea0b858f5d4cd825df1](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/ce320914f6c243e1b38299ebd6b26ddf/images/9e0829532c344ea0b858f5d4cd825df1Spencer_PPT11.png)![dafb9ce4e5734d26adc2b7efc4a0cd12](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/ce320914f6c243e1b38299ebd6b26ddf/images/dafb9ce4e5734d26adc2b7efc4a0cd12Spencer_PPT12.png)**Implementation (Unreal Engine 5)**

  * Import using CC Auto Setup; retarget to UE5 skeleton; adjust materials to use ID maps so I can recolor outfits in material instances without extra texture sets.

  * Create Chaos Cloth Assets for real-time garments using the Cloth Panel Editor; import USD; transfer skin weights maps; paint weight maps; create stretch/bend/mass/damping simulation configs based on exported USD data, create a lightweight physics collider for robust body interaction; tweak, refine, and iterate until the simulation looks right. Remesh sim/render mesh for performance.




![e33663a2bca24ddda12caaeb30a18668](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/ce320914f6c243e1b38299ebd6b26ddf/images/e33663a2bca24ddda12caaeb30a18668Spencer_PPT13.png)![dfb87522e87544aebeb3e4520588894b](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/ce320914f6c243e1b38299ebd6b26ddf/images/dfb87522e87544aebeb3e4520588894bSpencer_PPT14.png)![62a1e93ec7434da7a1aba5bf58ee11a5](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/ce320914f6c243e1b38299ebd6b26ddf/images/62a1e93ec7434da7a1aba5bf58ee11a5Spencer_PPT15.png)

  * Playable Character Blueprint for adding the cloth to the skeletal mesh, tweak LOD rules, and assign colours so the same character can be used in co-op with a different palette.

  * Add the Kawaii Physics plugin to the Animation Blueprint for lightweight secondary motion (hair bits, hood, small accessories) where full cloth would be overkill.




# **We also noticed that you utilized Unreal Engine's Chaos Cloth Asset to achieve real-time cloth simulation based on the garment authored in Marvelous Designer. Do you have any tips and tricks for streamlining the process?**

Here’s the checklist I actually use:

### **Authoring & export sanity**

  * Match the bind pose across CC → MD → UE. A slight pose mismatch will make skin weight transfers a miserable and frustrating experience.

  * Centimeters everywhere; consistent axis on export; export with thickness and simulation in MD.




### **Chaos setup & iteration**

  * In UE 5.6, use the new Proxy Deformer node to bind specific verts/faces from the sim mesh to the render mesh for a much cleaner simulation. Use the Remesh node to drastically reduce poly counts on sim and/or render meshes without wrecking behavior - both are big wins for real-time performance budgets.

  * The Panel Cloth Editor makes it easier to assemble multi-piece outfits and refit garments as you iterate but they can be difficult to learn. The UE documentation and videos can help with this.

  * Test with short dance/turn/jump loops captured from real gameplay to catch snaggy folds inside the simulation window and iterate before testing in-game.




### **Performance & pragmatism**

  * Use Collection LODs on Chaos Asset Terminal with stricter Remesh settings for higher LODs. Disable simulation on the highest LOD and use this on weaker platforms.

  * Use Kawaii Physics for small “sway” details (scarves, tassels) and keep Chaos for hero garments.

  * Keep materials simple: leverage ID maps for colorways and decals to avoid extra texture sets.

  * Test on a variety of target platforms and optimize for a consistent frame rate




### **Common gotchas**

  * If you came from CC4, CC5 has better bind poses for UE5-friendly skeleton export and better retargeting - this reduces the rest-pose shenanigans when transferring skin weights in the panel editor.

  * If your USD imported garments looks weird/glassy inside the Panel Editor, double-check the material that it is using as sometimes it will default to ‘USDImportTranslucentMaterial’ which is less than ideal for clothing.




# **In what ways did Marvelous Designer support your production and help you achieve realistic cloth effects in the game?**

Two huge ways: **iteration speed** and**creating convincing secondary motion.**

**The pattern-based workflow** lets me create clothing quickly, then test motion with simulation passes before touching the game engine. That’s how Riff’s hoodie keeps its floppy charm while the dungaree straps whip on turns, and why The Manager’s jacket sells weight in spins without looking rubbery. 

![8f0ad295776f4fe8947783784ce4c677](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/ce320914f6c243e1b38299ebd6b26ddf/images/8f0ad295776f4fe8947783784ce4c677Screenshot%202025-04-25%20205829.png)![594ea056bc89421385b51be2fd91eaa9](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/ce320914f6c243e1b38299ebd6b26ddf/images/594ea056bc89421385b51be2fd91eaa9Screenshot%202025-04-25%20204942.png)![17cc79c51842439793bdc1715caabd72](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/ce320914f6c243e1b38299ebd6b26ddf/images/17cc79c51842439793bdc1715caabd72Screenshot%202025-04-25%20210620.png)![4304df91768c4341ae8bdda972e82b57](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/ce320914f6c243e1b38299ebd6b26ddf/images/4304df91768c4341ae8bdda972e82b57Screenshot%202025-04-25%20205043.png)

**Engine-friendly handoff**. Clean panels → clean UVs → clean ID maps, which makes materials simple and enables colour options without extra textures. Exporting USD & garment sim data gives me a dependable starting point for Chaos Cloth to reproduce the behavior I approved in MD without relying on heavy Alembic caches that balloon file sizes. 

![29581b64897142ab97e80f18c6c4ce3d](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/ce320914f6c243e1b38299ebd6b26ddf/images/29581b64897142ab97e80f18c6c4ce3dSpencer%20Video.gif)

**One-tool consistency.** I even authored Harmony’s boots in MD just to test a “single-package” workflow end-to-end by keeping the whole outfit in MD.

![abe5c870f27a4a81b347a7d1e8dcdf43](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/ce320914f6c243e1b38299ebd6b26ddf/images/abe5c870f27a4a81b347a7d1e8dcdf43Spencer%20shoes.gif)

title: Simulation undo, divided gizmo, pin points
content:
1. For example I accidentaly deleted the avatar, but when I want undo, the simulation usually does not respond, so I lost the simulated fabric. I can do undo one by one every editing steps, but not the simulation. It would be good if the simulation would be undoable. Even if I tweak the creases it would be very helpful.

  2. I like much better​ the divided gizmo, easier to control, and same as other 3d softwares. The united gizmo needs more precise clicks. The pin uses the W shortcut: click+W new pin, click+W on the same pin = delete the pin (this is useful)

By changing to divided gizmo, the pin became P, so click+P new pin point, but I click+P again the points in not deleted as with W, so I need to select manually and delete manually one by one the points (I dont want delete all of my pin). It seems a bug.

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi there, thank you for your feedback. It has been noted.
content_description: This web page aims to gather user feedback and suggestions for improving the simulation and gizmo functionality in 3D editing software, focusing on enhancing the undo capabilities and optimizing pin management for a more intuitive user experience.

title: [JP] Lura: バーチャルリアリティーにおける快適な空間デザイン
content:
## _VRChatで数多くのワールド制作、3Dデザイン、ディレクションを手掛ける3Dアーティスト、Lura (_[_@Lu_Ra_999_](https://x.com/Lu_Ra_999) _) 氏。  
_[ _QuickBrown Design Studio_](https://quickbrown.net/) _の代表でもある彼が、これまでのワールド／アセット制作における制作経験を語ります。_

##  _Lura氏がMarvelous Designerと共に行った、バーチャルリアリティ空間に「快適でリラックスできる空間」をデザインし、創造するための道のりを追います。_

* * *

![fd8089806d2645798188d95e31356747](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/953fe15334244aadbb9f6ea5ef164eec/images/fd8089806d2645798188d95e313567471-3.jpg)![c0e4ee0da2274902ba22c36b4a5934eb](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/953fe15334244aadbb9f6ea5ef164eec/images/c0e4ee0da2274902ba22c36b4a5934ebbackpack.jpg)

# **1\. アーティスト紹介**

私はVRChatを中心に、ワールド制作やアートディレクション、モデリング、アセット販売を行っているLuraです。  
リアルタイムで動作する3DCG空間の制作を得意としており、ゲームやVR向けに住空間やイベント会場などをデザインしています。

武蔵野美術大学を卒業後、ゲーム業界で働きながらVRChatでの創作活動を開始しました。  
バーチャルマーケットやShaderFesなどのイベントで建築アセットやギミック制作を経験し、2023年にフリーランスとして独立。現在はQuickBrown Design Studioとして活動しています。

* * *

# **2\. アートディレクションとビジュアルスタイル**

代表的な事例として、「LuminousHotel」ではラグジュアリーなホテル空間をテーマに、長時間滞在しても快適に過ごせるよう設計。手触りの良いギミックも多く盛り込みました。

また、280万人以上が訪問した「Floating Airship」では、布を多用して柔らかくリラックスできる空間を演出。VRでも「ぶつかっても痛くない」ような安心感を与えるデザインを目指しました。

私が常に意識しているのは「長時間過ごしても不快にならない空間」です。特にライティングにこだわり、落ち着いた雰囲気を重視。VRではオブジェクトを至近距離で観察できるため、違和感を感じさせない精度で仕上げることを大切にしています。

* * *

# **3\. Marvelous Designerを用いた制作パイプラインと工夫**

#### **【ワールド制作での活用事例：Floating Airship】**

  1. **ワールドメッシュのインポート  
** Marvelous Designerでは既存のワールドのメッシュをそのまま取り込めるため、「Floating Airship」の空間をインポートして活用していました。




 _Floating AirshipをMarvelous Designerに取り込んだ際の画像_  
![af120b968eb84f68a1249aa04c6b4d5d](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/953fe15334244aadbb9f6ea5ef164eec/images/af120b968eb84f68a1249aa04c6b4d5d1-0.jpg)  


  2. **布や布団の物理演算配置  
** 取り込んだ空間内に布や布団を物理演算で自然に配置することで、柔らかくリラックスできる雰囲気を実現しています。




 _空間に布や布団を物理演算で配置_  
![2659b1b071664681a990f03e492172bb](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/953fe15334244aadbb9f6ea5ef164eec/images/2659b1b071664681a990f03e492172bb1-1.jpg)

  3. **完成形  
** 最終的に布の配置が空間全体の雰囲気を高め、居心地の良い滞在空間に仕上がりました。




 _完成した空間  
_![f990cd34979a453dbdc4bb8ba7e4791f](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/953fe15334244aadbb9f6ea5ef164eec/images/f990cd34979a453dbdc4bb8ba7e4791f1-3.jpg)

* * *

# **【プロップ制作での活用事例：リュックサック】**

  1. **Marvelous Designerでのモデリング  
** リュックサックをMarvelous Designer上で制作しました。内部に空気を入れるような調整ができ、中身が詰まった自然なシルエットを表現可能です。  
この段階では厚み付けは行わず、そのままBlenderへエクスポートします。




 _Marvelous Designerで完成したリュックサック_

![f41d31269f5a46d59cac47609fcc25cc](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/953fe15334244aadbb9f6ea5ef164eec/images/f41d31269f5a46d59cac47609fcc25cc2-1.jpg)  


  2. **Blenderでの調整  
** 厚みのない状態でBlenderに取り込み、まずトポロジーを整えます。Marvelous Designerで型紙の角を丸めるとトポロジーが複雑になりやすいため、平面のままQuadRemesherをかけてクリーンなトポロジーを確保。その後、厚み付けモディファイアで必要な部分に厚みを追加します。




 _Blenderに取り込んだ際の画像_

![a764dcb1345b4f6fb6b2566f0bae1e67](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/953fe15334244aadbb9f6ea5ef164eec/images/a764dcb1345b4f6fb6b2566f0bae1e672-2-1.jpg)  
 _QuadRemesherでトポロジーを綺麗にして厚み付けした際の画像_

![9a8be7165f5844ce8429f00a7c14ef9c](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/953fe15334244aadbb9f6ea5ef164eec/images/9a8be7165f5844ce8429f00a7c14ef9c2-2-2.png)

  3. **UV展開  
** トポロジーを綺麗にすることで、厚み付け後のUV展開がスムーズになります。




 _UV展開の全体画像_

![a53f5e3be9fb4c0bb47939ff6ca0f6de](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/953fe15334244aadbb9f6ea5ef164eec/images/a53f5e3be9fb4c0bb47939ff6ca0f6de2-3.png)

リュックの制作では、**UV1** と**UV2** を明確に役割分担しています。

* * *

##### **■ UV1（テクスチャ用）**

  * **目的** ：Substance Painterでの質感表現を正しく出すため

  * **方法** ：布の面と厚み部分を分離し、特に厚み部分は「直線的」に展開

  * **利点** ：曲率マップやエッジマップが綺麗に働き、縫い目の汚れや角の摩耗を自然に追加できる。厚み部分が直線化されているとペイント時の歪みも防げる。




 _UV1（布面＋厚み部分を直線化した展開）_  
![8eb1f8931c864d08976fcc910a256ec8](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/953fe15334244aadbb9f6ea5ef164eec/images/8eb1f8931c864d08976fcc910a256ec82-4.png)

* * *

##### **■ UV2（ライトマップ用）**

  * **目的** ：Unityでライトマップベイクした際の破綻防止

  * **方法** ：布の面と厚み部分をつなげて展開し、シームを目立たなくする

  * **利点** ：UV1のように分離すると解像度不足で縫い目に影やノイズが出やすいため、UV2ではなるべく連続的に展開。多少伸びてもライティング上は自然に見える。




 _UV2（布面と側面をつなげて展開）_  


![f6681d2f046543739a9c243d598f07ca](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/953fe15334244aadbb9f6ea5ef164eec/images/f6681d2f046543739a9c243d598f07ca2-5.png)

* * *

  4. **テクスチャリング（Substance Painter）  
** UV1を丁寧に展開しておくことで、曲率マップが正しく機能。エッジに汚しや色の変化を加えることで質感を大幅に高められます。  





 _Substance Painterでの画像（前面）  
_![66ce90d536354b859ef33d0962c5fa0f](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/953fe15334244aadbb9f6ea5ef164eec/images/66ce90d536354b859ef33d0962c5fa0f2-6-1.jpg)

 _Substance Painterでの画像（背面）_  


![b96f3088a1844a3baa1a20ac4081024e](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/953fe15334244aadbb9f6ea5ef164eec/images/b96f3088a1844a3baa1a20ac4081024e2-6-2.jpg)

* * *

MarvelousDesignerをリアルタイム環境で使う場合は、先の工程を意識しながら制作を進めることが重要です。
content_description: このウェブページでは、VRChatを中心に活動する3DアーティストLura氏が、Marvelous Designerを用いた快適でリラックスできるバーチャルリアリティ空間のデザイン過

title: [EN] Lura: Designing Comfortableness in Virtual Reality
content:
## _Meet Lura (_[_@Lu_Ra_999_](https://x.com/Lu_Ra_999) _) - 3D Artist, World Designer, and Director for world creation in VRChat._

## _As the director of_[ _QuickBrown Design Studio_](https://quickbrown.net/) _, Lura shares his story of using Marvelous Designer for world/asset creation: a journey of designing and creating a comfortable, relaxing space within virtual reality._

* * *

  
![a5e8966cb2064b99992b694ca653c662](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/78f7f40b240a49019ba8dad9d0f81325/images/a5e8966cb2064b99992b694ca653c6621-3.jpg)

![71f7c4465ccb42b0b0e53af4f07bbe68](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/78f7f40b240a49019ba8dad9d0f81325/images/71f7c4465ccb42b0b0e53af4f07bbe68backpack.jpg)

# **1\. Artist Introduction**

My name is Lura, an artist primarily active in VRChat, where I engage in world creation, art direction, modeling, and asset sales.  
I specialize in creating 3DCG spaces that operate in real-time, designing living spaces and event venues for video games and VR.   
  
After graduating from Musashino Art University, I began my creative activities in VRChat while working in the game industry. After gaining experience creating architectural assets and gimmicks for events such as Virtual Market and ShaderFes, I became a freelancer in 2023.   
I currently operate under the name “QuickBrown Design Studio.”

* * *

# **2\. Art Direction and Visual Style**

A representative example of my work is "Luminous Hotel," which was designed around the theme of a luxury hotel space, intended to be comfortable for extended stays.   
This world also includes many pleasant gimmicks.

For "Floating Airship," which has been visited by over 2.8 million people, I used cloth extensively to create a soft and relaxing atmosphere. I aimed for a design that would feel reassuring in VR, as like to “remove the sharp edges.”

I am always conscious of creating "a space that doesn't become uncomfortable even after spending a long time." I am particularly focusing on lighting, to emphasize a calm atmosphere. In VR, users can observe objects at very close range, so I finish my work with a level of precision that avoids any sense of uneasiness.

* * *

# **3\. Production Pipeline and Techniques Using Marvelous Designer**

**[Use Case in World Creation: Floating Airship]**

  1. **Importing the World Mesh**  
Since Marvelous Designer allows the creator to import existing world meshes as they are, I imported the space from "Floating Airship" to work with.  
_Image of Floating Airship imported into Marvelous Designer_![55e43f4c6b8048689ea3be9897930bfe](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/78f7f40b240a49019ba8dad9d0f81325/images/55e43f4c6b8048689ea3be9897930bfe1-0.jpg) _  
_

  2. **Physics-Based Placement of Cloth and Futon mattresses**  
By using physics simulations to naturally arrange cloth and futons within the imported space, I was able to achieve a soft and relaxing atmosphere.  
_Image of cloth and futons being placed in the space with physics_  
![5c68f2cc459c499390d8224b25f2ea81](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/78f7f40b240a49019ba8dad9d0f81325/images/5c68f2cc459c499390d8224b25f2ea811-1.jpg)

  3. **Completed Form**  
In the completed space, the cloth arrangement enhanced the overall atmosphere of the space, resulting in a comfortable and inviting environment.  
![941bb29c89eb494d982cd8a43cab5ce5](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/78f7f40b240a49019ba8dad9d0f81325/images/941bb29c89eb494d982cd8a43cab5ce51-3.jpg)




* * *

# **[Use Case in Asset Creation: Backpack]**

  1. **Modeling in Marvelous Designer**  
I created a backpack asset using Marvelous Designer. On Marvelous Designer, it's possible to make precise adjustments as if inflating it with air, which allows for the expression of a natural silhouette that looks like it's packed with items.   
I did not add thickness at this stage, which I exported directly to Blender.  
  
_Completed backpack in Marvelous Designer  
_![26c0178253ca407f83c52cb4dd8810aa](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/78f7f40b240a49019ba8dad9d0f81325/images/26c0178253ca407f83c52cb4dd8810aa2-1.jpg) _  
Image of the model imported into Blender_

![6f7f4cc2085b4a789e235fb88df34e4f](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/78f7f40b240a49019ba8dad9d0f81325/images/6f7f4cc2085b4a789e235fb88df34e4f2-2-1.jpg)  
 _Image after cleaning the topology with QuadRemesher and adding thickness_  
  
![8a71ddcb55f2499dbd2e0aeda92d0c2e](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/78f7f40b240a49019ba8dad9d0f81325/images/8a71ddcb55f2499dbd2e0aeda92d0c2e2-2-2.png) _  
_

  2. **Adjustments in Blender**  
I imported the model into Blender without any thickness and first cleaned up the topology. Rounding the corners of patterns in Marvelous Designer tends to complicate the topology, so I run QuadRemesher on it while it's still a flat plane to ensure a clean topology. Afterward, I use the Solidify modifier to add thickness where needed.  
_Image of the model imported into Blender_  
![072141ee0b154a2e888b4dc5115ce98f](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/78f7f40b240a49019ba8dad9d0f81325/images/072141ee0b154a2e888b4dc5115ce98f2-2-1.jpg)




 _Image after cleaning the topology with QuadRemesher and adding thickness  
_![65cc5d46974246b18cfc6801e6f701ed](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/78f7f40b240a49019ba8dad9d0f81325/images/65cc5d46974246b18cfc6801e6f701ed2-2-2.png)

  3. **UV Unwrapping**  
By cleaning up the topology beforehand, the UV unwrapping process after adding thickness becomes much smoother.  
_Overall image of the UV layout_

![1c65997953464c73a072e13b93923772](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/78f7f40b240a49019ba8dad9d0f81325/images/1c65997953464c73a072e13b939237722-3.png)

 _  
_For creating this backpack, I clearly divided the roles between**UV1** and **UV2**.




* * *

  * **UV1 (For Textures)**

    * **Purpose:** To ensure proper texture expression in Substance Painter.

    * **Method:** Separate the cloth faces from the thickness-added parts. Specifically, unwrap the thickness parts to be "straight."

    * **Advantage:** This allows curvature and edge maps to work cleanly, making it possible to naturally add dirt in the seams or wear on the corners. Straightening the thickness parts also prevents distortion during painting.  
_UV1 (Unwrap with cloth faces + straightened thickness parts)  
_![d75927230be14f96bd8858338021df77](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/78f7f40b240a49019ba8dad9d0f81325/images/d75927230be14f96bd8858338021df772-4.png)




* * *

  * **■ UV2 (For Lightmaps)**

    * **Purpose:** To prevent artifacts when baking lightmaps in Unity.

    * **Method:** Unwrap the cloth faces and thickness parts as connected pieces to make seams less noticeable.

    * **Advantage:** Separating them like in UV1 can lead to shadows and noise appearing in the seams due to insufficient resolution. Therefore, for UV2, I unwrap them as continuously as possible. A little stretching is acceptable as it tends to look natural in the final lighting.  
_UV2 (Unwrap with cloth faces and side parts connected)  
_




![8ca7dadbada440eabf79f2fc4731ab04](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/78f7f40b240a49019ba8dad9d0f81325/images/8ca7dadbada440eabf79f2fc4731ab042-5.png)

* * *

  4. **Texturing (Substance Painter)**  
By carefully unwrapping UV1, the curvature map functions correctly. This allows me to significantly enhance the texture by adding dirt and color variations to the edges.  
_Image from Substance Painter (Front)  
_![158643ac586c461ab4e26df6d5e06d68](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/78f7f40b240a49019ba8dad9d0f81325/images/158643ac586c461ab4e26df6d5e06d682-6-1.jpg)_  
Image from Substance Painter (Back)  
_![2a9a6e72d749470f9db097303262ea4c](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/78f7f40b240a49019ba8dad9d0f81325/images/2a9a6e72d749470f9db097303262ea4c2-6-2.jpg)

When using Marvelous Designer for real-time environments, it is crucial to proceed with production while keeping these subsequent steps in mind.




* * *
content_description: Discover Lura's creative journey as a 3D artist and world designer, showcasing the art of crafting immersive and relaxing virtual spaces in VRChat using Marvelous Designer.

title: Death is a Beginning: Weaving the Ethereal Fabric of Rebirth with Marvelous Designer
content:
## ![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/4ec67a57e8124fb8be51de9abec64a7f/images/bad56517d19047e491facd34407b5cd0Eduardo_square.png)_For Eduardo, fabric is never just fabric; it is the living protagonist of his art. This 3D artist skillfully employs Marvelous Designer to bridge digital textiles with his powerful 2D illustrations. Delve into "Death is a Beginning"—his striking reinterpretation of La Lotería's iconic card La Muerte (‘Death’), where the ethereal drape is precisely crafted to guide the viewer's eye through a profound narrative of rebirth._

* * *

# ![7adf6a1674204bcf96463df9d583cccd](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/4ec67a57e8124fb8be51de9abec64a7f/images/7adf6a1674204bcf96463df9d583cccdeduardo-gala-artstation-01.jpg)**Interview with**[**Eduardo Gala**](https://www.artstation.com/eddgala)**|**[**Death is a Beginning**](https://www.artstation.com/artwork/NqVNBJ)**| 3D Artist & Illustrator**

* * *

# **Could you start by introducing yourself and the core idea behind this artwork?**

I am a 3D artist and illustrator, and I truly enjoy using Marvelous Designer to achieve more refined and realistic fabric details in my illustrations. The software allows me to simulate natural elements such as wind, which brings greater credibility and dynamism to my characters.   
I am currently working on a series of illustrations inspired by a traditional Mexican game called**_La Lotería_**. One of its iconic cards is **_La Muerte_ (‘Death’).**

![61b733552d8c4d44b46a05bc75bdb85c](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/4ec67a57e8124fb8be51de9abec64a7f/images/61b733552d8c4d44b46a05bc75bdb85cimage.png)

If you look at the original card, it depicts a simple skeleton holding a scythe. For my reinterpretation, I wanted to give it a deeper meaning. 

![795f86748bea48fab50291d23294ab78](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/4ec67a57e8124fb8be51de9abec64a7f/images/795f86748bea48fab50291d23294ab78image.png)

To me, death does not represent the end of a story, but rather the beginning of something new. I believe in the idea of reincarnation, and that life is made of experiences we are meant to live and learn from. My illustration reflects that belief: it portrays a character who is about to reincarnate into a new version of themselves.

# **The composition is very powerful. Could you walk us through your thought process for creating this specific scene?**

For this piece, I used a centered composition surrounded by arches of _cempasúchil_ flowers. In Mexico, we celebrate the Day of the Dead on November 2nd, and we decorate the graves of our loved ones with altars made of _cempasúchil_ , similar to what many people saw in the film _Coco_.

![99da41eba3a44e09a9574e5a3c0b7ad1](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/4ec67a57e8124fb8be51de9abec64a7f/images/99da41eba3a44e09a9574e5a3c0b7ad1image.png)

![9eba50f0c0a84a1fb0117f2a9f12bc1b](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/4ec67a57e8124fb8be51de9abec64a7f/images/9eba50f0c0a84a1fb0117f2a9f12bc1byellow-flower-with-background-yellow-flowers-out-focus.jpg)

For the character of Death, I dressed her in black to symbolize mourning, while the new soul is dressed in white to represent a beginning. The dress of Death dissolves into butterflies, which then start to form the body of the new soul.

![f73b72ccda214313b7767eb9d690937b](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/4ec67a57e8124fb8be51de9abec64a7f/images/f73b72ccda214313b7767eb9d690937beduardo-gala-artstation-02.jpg)

# **What role did Marvelous Designer play in the creation of this artwork? Which elements were designed using Marvelous Designer?**

I always plan my compositions in Unreal Engine, which requires a 3D mesh that I can integrate into the software. Marvelous Designer allows me to arrange the fabrics, experiment with**wind simulations** , and even adjust the type of material, giving me more creative control. 

![9e1f4a97e01e47869e219b3189cb2bc9](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/4ec67a57e8124fb8be51de9abec64a7f/images/9e1f4a97e01e47869e219b3189cb2bc9Eduardo%20Recording_MD1.gif)![16c2c53ba7de4c8097dd30e6870532ff](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/4ec67a57e8124fb8be51de9abec64a7f/images/16c2c53ba7de4c8097dd30e6870532ffEduardo_wind2.gif)

YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KYoRar_zIwQ?start=0

In this particular piece, I wanted the dress to appear as if it were dissolving, so I used wind simulation in Marvelous to achieve the initial effect. Later, when I moved the work into Photoshop, I refined the illustration by gradually disintegrating the dress using masks. 

# **Could you describe your process for creating this element inside Marvelous Designer?**

Previously, I worked as a character artist, and as many know, in that field fabrics needed to be perfectly clean and functional so that the character could later be textured and prepared for production.

Now that I focus on illustration, I feel I have much more creative freedom. I can place and pose the fabrics, add objects so they adapt to very specific positions, and really experiment.

That’s exactly what I did for this piece: I used wind simulation and manually adjusted the fabric until the folds appeared exactly where I wanted them to enhance the composition.

![2aeb2bc7baa048d9978bc588532b668e](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/4ec67a57e8124fb8be51de9abec64a7f/images/2aeb2bc7baa048d9978bc588532b668eeduardo-gala-muerte-sketch-02.jpg)

![5c252f5868cc4904a6db50cf2240b29a](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/4ec67a57e8124fb8be51de9abec64a7f/images/5c252f5868cc4904a6db50cf2240b29aeduardo-gala-muerte-sketch-01.jpg)![b2736b32351f4776ab2ad22413704f42](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/4ec67a57e8124fb8be51de9abec64a7f/images/b2736b32351f4776ab2ad22413704f42eduardo-gala-muerte-sketch-08.jpg)

# **What were the biggest challenges you faced, and how did you overcome them?**

The most challenging part was controlling the level of detail in order to guide the viewer’s eye. I carefully arranged the fabric folds so they would work as visual guides leading toward the baby.

Another challenge was figuring out how the dress would dissolve, but I ultimately resolved that within the final composition.

![a06edf0697184326ba4621aa416f243b](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/4ec67a57e8124fb8be51de9abec64a7f/images/a06edf0697184326ba4621aa416f243bEduardo_transparent%20.png)![773006817c304944aeec64b4e663f4ce](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/4ec67a57e8124fb8be51de9abec64a7f/images/773006817c304944aeec64b4e663f4ceEduardo_transparent2.png)![66e0e92abb8b4b3da9399f8334233375](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/4ec67a57e8124fb8be51de9abec64a7f/images/66e0e92abb8b4b3da9399f8334233375eduardo_transparent3.png)![010b7829eb844ff69ebd46608a6ce9b5](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/4ec67a57e8124fb8be51de9abec64a7f/images/010b7829eb844ff69ebd46608a6ce9b5eduardo_transparent%205.png)

# **Are there any particular features in Marvelous Designer that you find indispensable for bringing your surreal and highly detailed character concepts to life?**

The wind, being able to pose the fabric in real time, and pins are my best friends in this process.

![86718d4eeff54ed5808d14a450d296cd](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/4ec67a57e8124fb8be51de9abec64a7f/images/86718d4eeff54ed5808d14a450d296cdEduardo_Wind.gif)

# **Could you give us an overview of your entire workflow for this piece?**

YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SyI4hIhyu0s?start=0

# **How does your work in Marvelous Designer integrate with the rest of your 3D/2D pipeline?**

My characters usually require a large amount of fabric, and over time **fabric has become the true protagonist of my work**. I often design them with heavy robes that cover their bodies, and having precise control over how the garments are posed is essential for me. 

**In my process, fabric plays a key role in guiding the viewer’s eye, so I need to direct it exactly where I want the audience to focus.**

This is why Marvelous Designer is more useful for me than other software, such as ZBrush, where I cannot preview results as quickly or make detailed adjustments to folds and wrinkles with the same efficiency.

![89c75f10b80948f29be1f50e28802e7c](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/4ec67a57e8124fb8be51de9abec64a7f/images/89c75f10b80948f29be1f50e28802e7ceduardo-gala-muerte-sketch-04.jpg)

# **What advice would you give to other artists who want to use Marvelous Designer not just for realistic clothing, but for creating fantastical and symbolic garments like the one in your piece?**

When illustrating, it’s crucial to have a clear vision of what you want to communicate with every element in the scene.

**If you are using Marvelous Designer to pose clothing, don’t think of the garments as just clothing, they can also guide the viewer’s eye and help describe your characters.**

That’s why it’s important to start with a sketch, marking the points where you want to direct attention, and then design the clothing based on that sketch. 

# **How would you describe your overall experience using Marvelous Designer?**

The software is very nice and intuitive; it's my favorite part of pre-production composition.
